title: Walmart Supplier Requirements: 4 Steps to Becoming a Walmart Supplier
summary: Learn Walmart supplier requirements and the four steps to becoming a Walmart supplier, from registration and documentation to EDI setup and onboarding.
body_markdown:
In this article, learn about:


-


The key differences between being a Walmart supplier and a Marketplace seller


-


The Walmart supplier requirements and the four steps to meet them


-


Walmart's EDI requirements, the products Walmart buys, and other ways to get in front of a buyer


---


As many suppliers have learned, getting your products onto Walmart’s shelves starts long before the first purchase order arrives. Suppliers navigate a detailed onboarding process that includes business verification, product information, insurance,[electronic data interchange](https://www.spscommerce.com/what-is-edi/) (EDI), and signed agreements.


Walmart works with[more than 100,000 businesses worldwide](https://corporate.walmart.com/suppliers/apply-to-be-a-supplier) , and[more than 60% of its suppliers](https://corporate.walmart.com/suppliers/supplier-inclusion) are verified small businesses. Self-registering does not guarantee Walmart will offer you an agreement, so getting your information ready before you apply is the best way to avoid delays.


## What Are Walmart's Supplier Requirements?


Walmart's supplier requirements are the information, documents, and systems you must provide to finish onboarding in Retail Link. Per Walmart's[supplier onboarding checklist](https://corporate.walmart.com/content/dam/corporate/documents/suppliers/apply-to-be-a-supplier/supplier-checklist.pdf) , you need:


-


**A data universal numbering system (DUNS) number:** Walmart requires it for registration, and your legal name and address must match your IRS and tax form records.


-


**Tax forms:** U.S. suppliers submit a W-9. International suppliers submit a W-8.


-


**Product IDs:** List GTINs, UPCs, EANs, ISBNs, or your own SKUs, up to 200 items at a time, with a publicly accessible image URL for each product.


-


**Liability insurance:** Certificates must name Walmart as an additional insured party and certificate holder.


-


**An EDI connection:** Walmart's store and Sam's Club banners require EDI, covered in detail below.


-


**A U.S. bank account:** Domestic suppliers need a bank that accepts USD.


-


**Company contacts:** Add an administrator, CEO, and CFO first, then the other roles Walmart lists.


-


**Policy acknowledgments:** You review and accept Walmart's Standards for Suppliers, Code of Conduct, product safety, and related documents.


Walmart can change its requirements at any time, so confirm them against the current checklist before you apply.


## What Is the Difference Between a Walmart Supplier and a Marketplace Seller?


A Walmart supplier sells to Walmart. Walmart buys the product, sends purchase orders, and resells the item in its stores and on Walmart.com. A Marketplace seller sells directly to shoppers on Walmart.com and is responsible for its own products and orders.


The two paths can look alike at the start, but they work differently once you are in.

**Marketplace seller**

For a closer look at both models, read[What Is a Walmart Seller vs. Supplier?](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/what-is-a-walmart-seller-vs-supplier) or[First Steps to Sell on Walmart Marketplace](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/first-steps-to-sell-on-walmart-marketplace) . The Walmart supplier requirements in this guide apply to the supplier path.


## What Are the Four Steps to Becoming a Walmart Supplier?


The four steps are to create a Retail Link account, submit your company, tax, and product information, complete the rest of Walmart's onboarding dashboard, and accept the supplier agreements.


### Step 1: Create Your Retail Link Account


Start on Walmart's[Apply to be a Supplier](https://corporate.walmart.com/suppliers/apply-to-be-a-supplier) page. Review the supplier checklist, then select Create Account in Retail Link to begin qualification.


During registration, you choose where your products will sell: Walmart, Sam's Club, Walmart.com, or SamsClub.com. That choice shapes your EDI setup later.


### Step 2: Submit Company, Tax, and Product Information


Three sections come first: company information, tax information, and product submission. You provide your legal name, address, entity type, and remittance address, plus your tax ID and W-9 or W-8.


For products, you download a spreadsheet template, add your product IDs and details, and upload it. Walmart notes that incorrect information delays your vendor agreement, so check each entry before you submit.


### Step 3: Complete the Rest of the Onboarding Dashboard


Walmart's onboarding dashboard has more sections to finish before a merchant can send your Business Terms Agreement. They cover:


-


Contacts


-


Product and brand details, including brand IDs for in-store products and a food safety profile for food and produce


-


Insurance


-


EDI setup


-


Banking


-


Business certification


-


Logistics and delivery details


-


Policy acknowledgments


Direct import suppliers also submit quotes and set up factory audits.


### Step 4: Accept the Supplier Agreements and Set Up Items


Walmart's supplier agreement has two parts: the Master Supplier Agreement and the Business Terms Agreement. The Master Supplier Agreement opens after your company, tax, and product sections are complete. You accept it before you can act on the Business Terms Agreement.


Read both carefully. They cover payment terms and compliance obligations. Accepting them is not a guarantee of business.


After you accept, upload your certificate of insurance in Retail Link within 30 days. Once you have a supplier number and at least one item set up, you leave onboarding and get full access to Retail Link and Walmart's Academy.


## What Are Walmart's EDI Requirements for New Suppliers?


Walmart requires suppliers selling to Walmart stores, Sam’s Club, and SamsClub.com to exchange business documents electronically through EDI. These documents include purchase orders,[advance ship notices](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/edi-856-ship-notice-manifest) (ASNs), and invoices.


Suppliers selling exclusively through Walmart.com use a different system called WebEDI. Walmart automatically creates a WebEDI mailbox after the supplier receives their agreement.


During onboarding, Walmart asks a few questions to determine which EDI setup your business needs. These include the types of documents you'll exchange, whether you're supplying products for resale, and whether you expect to exchange more than 15,000 documents annually.


Depending on your answers, Walmart may require Applicability Statement 2 (AS2), a secure method for sending EDI documents directly between computer systems over the internet. Suppliers handling pharmacy products, goods not intended for resale, or higher document volumes may need to use AS2.


Common Walmart EDI documents include the 850 purchase order, 855 purchase order acknowledgment, 860 purchase order change, 856 advance ship notice, 810 invoice, and 997 functional acknowledgment.[SPS Commerce](https://www.spscommerce.com/network/find-a-partner/view/walmart-usa/) supports Walmart EDI compliance, item setup, and POS data for vendors. See its[page on Walmart EDI compliance](https://www.spscommerce.com/network/find-a-partner/view/walmart-usa/) for the full document list.


### Do Food Suppliers Have Extra EDI Requirements?


Yes. Walmart expects all food suppliers to send an advance ship notice with key data elements for every shipment of food, in any channel. These requirements follow FSMA 204, and Walmart lists the[data elements](https://enablement.walmart.com/content/food-safety/en_us/food-safety-requirements/food-traceability.html) on its supplier enablement site.


**Related Reading:**[How Suppliers Can Connect with Walmart](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/how-suppliers-can-connect-with-walmart-from-first-contact-to-full-compliance)


## How Does Early Black Friday Affect Walmart Supplier Requirements?


Early Black Friday does not change Walmart's supplier requirements, but it raises the stakes for meeting them. Walmart's 2026[Early Black Friday Deals run November 12 to 15](https://retaildive.com/news/walmart-longer-black-friday-cyber-monday-sales-events/872747) , so November 14 falls inside the promotional period. Black Friday Deals follow November 23 to 29, and Cyber Monday deals run November 30 to December 2.


Promotions drive order volume, and retailers do not relax compliance rules to match it. SPS explains in[OTIF During Peak Season](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/otif-during-peak-season-how-to-protect-your-scorecard-when-volume-spikes) that Walmart holds suppliers to the same standards when volume spikes. Before the next event, confirm that:


-


Your items are set up and active in Retail Link


-


Your EDI connection is configured and tested


-


Your advance ship notices are accurate and sent on time


If you are still onboarding, treat these dates as a preview of the volume you will handle once your first orders arrive. The[Holiday Peak Season 2026 supplier readiness checklist](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/holiday-peak-season-2026-supplier-readiness-checklist) walks through what to review.


## What Products Does Walmart Buy From Suppliers?


Walmart buys general merchandise and grocery items from suppliers, and its stores and website carry competitively priced products customers prefer.


-


**General merchandise:** home fixtures, household items, health and beauty aids, pet supplies, sports goods, electronics, automotive, jewelry, toys, clothing, hardware, and gardening items


-


**Grocery:** dry goods and staples, canned and packaged goods, frozen foods, paper goods, deli foods, beverages, seasonings, fresh produce, meat and dairy products, and bakery goods


Once you are on board, you get exposure to Walmart's large customer base. In-store services such as restaurants, clinics, and salons follow a different path, covered next.


## What Other Ways Can You Get in Front of a Walmart Buyer?


The retail supplier application is the main route, but Walmart also points resale suppliers to discovery programs such as RangeMe, Marketplace, and Open Call.


### Walmart Open Call


Open Call is Walmart's annual event where U.S. entrepreneurs pitch products made, grown, or assembled in the United States to Walmart and Sam's Club buyers. Walmart held[Open Call 2026](https://corporate.walmart.com/suppliers/investing-in-american-jobs/events/annual-open-call/open-call-2026) in Bentonville on October 6 and 7, and it has committed to buy an additional $350 billion in U.S.-made products by January 2031.


**Related Reading:**[How to Prepare for Walmart's Open Call](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/how-to-prepare-for-walmarts-open-call)


### Service and Non-Resale Suppliers


If you offer services or products Walmart does not resell, use Walmart's[service and non-resale path](https://corporate.walmart.com/suppliers/apply-to-be-a-supplier/service-non-resale) . Businesses that want space inside a store can look at[in-store leasing](https://leasing.walmart.com/) .


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What are the main Walmart supplier requirements?


You need a DUNS number, a W-9 or W-8 tax form, product IDs for your catalog, liability insurance, an EDI connection, and a U.S. bank account. You also add company contacts, accept Walmart's policies, and sign the Master Supplier Agreement and Business Terms Agreement.


### Do I need EDI to become a Walmart supplier?


Yes, if you sell to Walmart stores, Sam's Club, or SamsClub.com. Suppliers that sell only on Walmart.com use WebEDI, which Walmart sets up after you receive your agreement.


### Do I need a DUNS number to register?


Yes. Walmart requires a DUNS number for registration. If you do not have one, you can request it from[Dun & Bradstreet](https://www.dnb.com/en-us/smb/duns.html) and tell them you are applying to become a Walmart supplier.


### Can a small business become a Walmart supplier?


Yes. In FY2025,[more than 60% of Walmart's suppliers](https://corporate.walmart.com/suppliers/supplier-inclusion) were small businesses verified under its Supplier Inclusion program. Registering does not guarantee Walmart will extend you an agreement.


### When do I have to submit proof of insurance?


You enter insurance information during onboarding, before you receive your Business Terms Agreement. After you accept the Supplier Agreement, you have 30 days to upload your certificate of insurance in Retail Link.
